g.data-description: the power button
g.title: power-btn

g.data-description: the power symbol itself, lit from behind. It is the glyph that lights, not a separate indicator beside it, which is why the element is the symbol's own box rather than a dot.
the front VGA, the USB-A and the iDRAC Direct micro-AB USB
g.title: usb-1

g.data-description: the front VGA, the USB-A and the iDRAC Direct micro-AB USB
g.title: idrac-direct

g.data-description: the front VGA, the USB-A and the iDRAC Direct micro-AB USB
g.title: vga

g.data-description: printed marks seated as parts - the USB, iDRAC Direct and VGA symbols and the panel's vent grid
g.title: mark-usb-1

g.data-description: printed marks seated as parts - the USB, iDRAC Direct and VGA symbols and the panel's vent grid
g.title: mark-idrac

g.data-description: printed marks seated as parts - the USB, iDRAC Direct and VGA symbols and the panel's vent grid
g.title: mark-vga

g.data-description: printed marks seated as parts - the USB, iDRAC Direct and VGA symbols and the panel's vent grid
g.title: panel-grid

g.data-description: R760 ISM table 181: solid green for two seconds when a laptop or tablet is connected, flashing green (two on, two off) when recognised, off when unplugged - the R740xd's table 8 word for word.
g.title: idrac-direct-led

g.data-description: the rack release levers, one built into each ear. Pressed to free the chassis from the rail, so they release the BOX rather than operating anything in it, which is why they are furniture
g.title: latch-left

rect.data-description: the pressed face at the top of the rocker, where the finger goes. Below it the moulding is a plain grip.

g.data-description: the rack release levers, one built into each ear. Pressed to free the chassis from the rail, so they release the BOX rather than operating anything in it, which is why they are furniture
g.title: latch-right

rect.data-description: the pressed face at the top of the rocker, where the finger goes. Below it the moulding is a plain grip.

g.data-description: the slide-out Express Service Tag under the right-hand drives
g.title: info-tag

g.data-description: the drive glyph, lit. ISM table 2 - solid amber if there is a drive error.
the thermometer glyph. Solid amber on a thermal error - ambient out of range, or a fan failure.
the lightning glyph. Solid amber on voltage out of range, a failed PSU or a failed voltage regulator.
the memory glyph. Solid amber on a memory error.
the PCIe glyph. Solid amber when a PCIe card errors.

rect.data-description: the system health and system ID bar, and the button that switches between the two modes: solid blue - on, healthy, ID mode not active; blinking blue - ID mode active; solid amber - fail-safe mode; blinking amber - a fault, check the event log. The codes are the R660's table 129 (dell/control-panel-left-16g@1). NO RATE IS PUBLISHED for either blink, so 1 Hz is this library's reading and is not a figure Dell states.

rect.data-states: off ready transfer updating disabled fail-safe unresponsive
rect.data-description: the iDRAC Quick Sync 2 bar, and the button that turns the feature on and off. Every code in the R660's table 130, at the shape that table gives (dell/control-panel-left-16g@1): off, solid and blinking white, five rapid blinks then off, solid and blinking amber. The 2.5 second tail of `disabled` is this library's reading of 'and then turns off'.

g.data-description: The pulse glyph, which is itself the lamp. Dell KB 000413096 puts the activity indicator on the left; the R740xd Owner's Guide says what it does - "The activity LED flashes whenever the drive is accessed" - so it BLINKS rather than sitting solid. NO RATE IS PUBLISHED and none is stated: access is not periodic, so a frequency here would be a decoration pretending to be a measurement.

g.data-states: off online identify failure rebuilding predicted-failure rebuild-aborted
g.data-description: The drive-cylinder glyph, which is itself the lamp. Every state from Dell KB 000413096, at the rate and in the sequence that article gives, and RAID configurations only as it says. `identify` blinks twice a second and `failure` four times: same amber-or-green question, different condition, and they are only distinguishable because the rate is carried. `predicted-failure` is green, amber, off with no timing published, so its phases divide evenly; `rebuild-aborted` has Dell's three, three and six seconds. `rebuilding` is 'blinks green slowly', and 0.5 Hz is this library's reading of slowly rather than a figure Dell states. `off` IS NOT ONLY AN EMPTY BAY: the Owner's Guide adds that the status indicator "remains off until all drives are initialized after the system is turned on", so a dark lamp on a running machine can also mean the array is still coming up.

The pulse glyph, which is itself the lamp. Dell KB 000413096 puts the activity indicator on the left; the R740xd Owner's Guide says what it does - "The activity LED flashes whenever the drive is accessed" - so it BLINKS rather than sitting solid. NO RATE IS PUBLISHED and none is stated: access is not periodic, so a frequency here would be a decoration pretending to be a measurement.

Every state from Dell KB 000413096, at the rate and in the sequence that article gives, and RAID configurations only as it says. `identify` blinks twice a second and `failure` four times: same amber-or-green question, different condition, and they are only distinguishable because the rate is carried. `predicted-failure` is green, amber, off with no timing published, so its phases divide evenly; `rebuild-aborted` has Dell's three, three and six seconds. `rebuilding` is 'blinks green slowly', and 0.5 Hz is this library's reading of slowly rather than a figure Dell states. `off` IS NOT ONLY AN EMPTY BAY: the Owner's Guide adds that the status indicator "remains off until all drives are initialized after the system is turned on", so a dark lamp on a running machine can also mean the array is still coming up.

The pulse glyph, which is itself the lamp. Dell KB 000413096 puts the activity indicator on the left; the R740xd Owner's Guide says what it does - "The activity LED flashes whenever the drive is accessed" - so it BLINKS rather than sitting solid. NO RATE IS PUBLISHED and none is stated: access is not periodic, so a frequency here would be a decoration pretending to be a measurement.

the system cover and the backplane cover on top, and the optional security bezel on the front. The bezel is DRAWN FITTED, as on the R740xd and R660: it is `mounts`, so the viewer takes it off to show the drives, and `for:` names what it covers.

g.title: bezel

path.data-description: the bezel - end plates and honeycomb - over an open ground

circle.data-description: the keylock - unlocked with the bezel key before the bezel comes off (ISM 'Removing the front bezel', step 1).

rect.data-description: the release button on the left end plate - step 2 of removal, pressed before the left end is pulled away.
